name: Maurrassisme
summary: Maurrassisme is the doctrine of Charles Maurras and Action française: an integral nationalism holding that France can be restored only through a hereditary, anti-parliamentary and decentralized monarchy. It puts politics first, rejects democracy, liberalism and the Revolution, values Catholicism as social order rather than as faith, and treats Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as 'anti-France'.
scope: Maurras's doctrine as set out in Enquête sur la monarchie (1900) and the Action française movement from 1899 to about 1945, including its corporatist and national-syndicalist leanings and its support of Vichy. Excludes later neo-Maurrassian groups; modern questions are inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Maurras is described as opposed to capitalism and as corporatist and dirigiste, so he would not trust markets over state and corporate direction.

unions-good.rationale: Action française took up national syndicalism and corporations but opposed class-struggle unionism, so adherents split on unions as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: He opposed communism and class politics; corporatist cooperation between owners and workers keeps existing ownership, an inference rather than a stated position.

state-harmful.rationale: He wants a strong state with authority at the top; anarchism is the opposite of his doctrine.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: His authoritarian nationalism backed order and the military, and his Camelots du Roi acted as a paramilitary force.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: One of the four principles of his monarchy is decentralization: the king at the top with local and regional liberties below.

traditional-family.rationale: The family appears with locality, work and parish as part of the pays réel on which he wanted society to rest.

more-religion-public.rationale: He prized Catholicism as a social glue though agnostic himself, and the movement backed restoring it as state religion after 1905.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He judges French questions from the standpoint of France and finds no political framework wider than the nation; tradition is the heart of his doctrine.

gradual-change.rationale: Organizing empiricism: institutions should come from centuries of experience, though he accepted a coup to restore the monarchy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He holds that no political framework exists wider than the nation and attacked humanitarian utopianism.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is the sole political frame and 'France d'abord' was his guiding line, including under Vichy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He condemned 'l'utopie humanitaire' and put national interest first.

open-borders.rationale: His doctrine excludes foreigners as anti-France and rests on rooted national community.

revolution-justified.rationale: He blamed the 1789 Revolution for France's decline and was counter-revolutionary, though he planned a royalist coup.

central-planning.rationale: Dirigiste but corporatist and anti-communist; no support for full central planning is documented.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His organic society of trades, families and localities favors broad rooted ownership, but he did not state it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He was staunchly opposed to communism.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism is named in his doctrine and Enquête sur la monarchie refers readers to La Tour du Pin's corporatist writings for the social order.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wanted a hereditary king, not a ruling party, and the League was a pressure movement, not a state party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a monarch who rules, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state, on which the sources cited here are silent.

reviewHistory.rationale: Hereditary monarchy is the keystone of his doctrine; heredity ties the dynasty's interest to the nation's.

democracy-best.rationale: He rejected democratic principles as contrary to natural inequality and blamed democracy for national decline.

direct-votes.rationale: He rejected popular sovereignty and democracy; local and corporate representation was his only accepted form.

workers-councils.rationale: Opposed to communism and class-based rule; the base would be family, locality and trade under a king.

right-to-secede.rationale: He wanted regional liberties inside a unified France under the king, not secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: He held democracy contradicts natural inequality and defended dynastic rule trained from childhood.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Camelots du Roi practised street violence and he theorized a coup d'état and called for killings of opponents.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement backed restoring Catholicism as state religion after the 1905 separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: His politics rested on reason, tradition and natural law, with Catholicism valued as social order rather than revelation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A strong centralized royal authority over justice and defence is part of his model.

military-superiority.rationale: He was hostile to Germany, demanded a harsh Versailles, and backed national strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He rejected scientific racism and defined the nation by history and tradition, though he excluded Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He rejected communism and class struggle in favour of national solidarity under the king.

equal-outcomes.rationale: His doctrine centres on natural inequality and hierarchy.

civilizational-union.rationale: He recognised no framework wider than the nation, though a Latin or Catholic civilizational sympathy existed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His organic view puts national and corporate duties above individualism, though he never addressed the claim directly.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rejected abstract individual rights for organic duties to family, locality, trade and nation as in the pays réel.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalists of this era feared depopulation; not specifically documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: He held France had declined since 1789 and wanted the monarchy back; his restoration is organizing empiricism, though framed as renewal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Organizing empiricism: institutions are judged by historical experience, not abstract theory, though he was doctrinaire.

direct-action.rationale: He theorized leagues and extra-parliamentary action, including a coup, instead of elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: He accepted violent and coercive means for a restored order.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to a rupture with tradition and civilization; classical and Catholic culture is his ideal.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: His corporatist order rests on trades and hierarchy.

production-for-use.rationale: Opposed to communism; corporatist order is not use-based planning.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory contradicts his rejection of class struggle.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He was staunchly opposed to communism and to class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Rooted local and family ownership is closer to his pays réel; collectivism is rejected as communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory is rejected; he attributed war to republican weakness and German power.

taxation-theft.rationale: He wanted a strong state, with assemblies consenting to taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: His authoritarian traditionalism allows the state to enforce moral and national order.

individual-rights-only.rationale: His organic view of communities and the nation rejects individualist rights.

conscription.rationale: He backed national defence and the military against Germany.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit is incompatible with his rooted, nation-first outlook.

state-as-business.rationale: Rejects a customer model of the state; the state is an organic patrimony.

hereditarian-race.rationale: He rejected scientific racism, so he would not ground ability in race.

organic-representation.rationale: Enquête sur la monarchie wants councils and assemblies of corporations, family and locality, and refers to La Tour du Pin's corporatism.

total-state.rationale: His monarchy decentralizes and leaves local and corporate liberties; authority is strong but not total.

national-rebirth.rationale: He held France was in decline since 1789 and the monarchy would restore national greatness.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposed colonial expansion as a distraction from Germany, so not clear.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on a hereditary dynasty and law, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of his corporatist order.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He appealed to natural order and reason.

universal-morality.rationale: He appealed to natural law but made nationalism the horizon.

single-common-good.rationale: He held that the nation's good is a single end of politics, set against party competition.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democracy rejected; corporatist bodies and authority instead.

rule-by-example.rationale: He wanted a trained heir, but also laws and councils.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The monarchy is presented as a theorem, scientific and reasoned, not revealed.

class-collaboration.rationale: He called for national solidarity and corporatism opposing class struggle, with the king as keystone.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Tradition and inherited institutions are valued.

workers-nation.rationale: Action française combined integral nationalism with national syndicalism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He rejected scientific racism, though he favored state action against the Jews as a group.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement theory is later; he distrusted Jews and foreigners but his thought centred on republican elites.

national-mission.rationale: He wanted France restored for itself rather than spreading its government abroad, and opposed colonial adventure as a diversion, leaving this neutral.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He attacked the Republic's politicians as putting party above nation, the pays légal against the pays réel.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He rejected scientific racism; excluded groups by 'anti-France'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Maurras rejected the egalitarianism of 1789 as a destructive abstraction and called for excluding Jews and other 'confederated states' from the national community; he valued Catholicism for order, not for its doctrine of equal dignity.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The movement backed restoring Catholic position, opposing laïque schooling.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy rests on reason and heredity, not popular sovereignty or social contract.

population-transfer.rationale: He supported state anti-Semitism and criticized Vichy's 1940 Jewish statute as too moderate.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He backed street violence and a coup.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social-Darwinist competition between peoples was not his framework; he stressed order, tradition and cooperation, and sources do not decide it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He accepted state repression of the 'anti-France' and himself was repressed under the Republic.

separated-powers.rationale: He wanted a king who reigns and governs, not checks by deputies, though councils would provide advice and consent.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Corporatism seeks to replace conflict between classes by corporate bodies.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His exclusion of Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners rested on cohesion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He supported strong authority against internal enemies and backed Vichy.

party-controls-media.rationale: He wanted royal authority, not a ruling party; he himself was subject to press censorship.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army would be under the king.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: He wanted councils and assemblies under a king, not pay rules for representatives, so there is nothing to answer.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: No political framework wider than the nation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A king who reigns and governs, as in the Enquête, commands the state including the army.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maurras was agnostic and valued the Church as an instrument for national order, not as a ruler.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He supported union nationale in 1914 and 1940.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A hereditary king serves for life.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He supported alliance diplomacy against Germany.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The pays réel of locality, parish, family.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: His critique targeted the republican political class rather than university graduates, and he was himself an intellectual, so neutral.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He held France and the classical tradition higher.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: His nation is built on historic continuity, but he did not state a citizenship rule.

minority-language-support.rationale: As a Provençal regionalist he valued regional cultural liberties.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He excluded minorities like Protestants as anti-France.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social cohesion and tradition are prized.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonization economics is outside his doctrine; he did not see political order as needing property transformation, so a mild disagreement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He rejected popular sovereignty; the monarchy is restored not voted in.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rapid development is not his theme; he supported strong authority, but for national restoration rather than growth, so neutral.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Hereditary succession in place of election is his keystone.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not in his writings, so neutral.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The king above parties unifying the nation is core to his argument against partisan republic.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Legitimacy is rational not divine right.

character-from-environment.rationale: His thought stressed inheritance of tradition and natural inequality, though he also relied on upbringing in training a dynastic heir, so a weak disagreement.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He blamed Louis XIV's absolutism, wanted a king bound by councils.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He wanted a king with councils, not strictly a mixed regime.

leader-cult.rationale: He criticized fascist cults though he valued Pétain.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: No wider framework than the nation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He opposed Marxism, attributing decline to politics, hence 'Politics first'.

ban-cartels.rationale: He distrusted liberal finance but his corporatist order would organize industry in bodies, not break them up, so neutral.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not in his writings; he valued duty and national devotion but gave no incentive system.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Camelots du Roi and the coup d'état plans.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Heredity is the keystone of the monarchy; hereditary institutions defended.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He opposed assimilationist colonialism but favored empire.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Institut d'Action française gave an alternative education.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Maurras was no theorist of capitalist crisis, so neutral.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He supported French empire but wrote little on postcolonial influence, so neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian private-association rights are not his framework; he favored state action against excluded groups, so a mild disagreement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Heredity rather than election is the keystone.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The dynasty is expected to be bound by its own interest, not popular resistance.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School theme; Maurras's culture critique blamed romanticism and the Revolution, so neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim outside his doctrine, and he rejected class analysis, so a weak disagreement.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist parties on which he had no stake, so neutral.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist stance on Versailles toward Germany.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He opposed communism and Nazism but not the authoritarian state.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical question that his sources never touch, so neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Organizing empiricism: institutions arise from a nation's own history.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Maurras's circle courted army and coup.

filial-duty.rationale: Family is part of the pays réel.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Enquête wants assemblies consenting to taxes but not parliamentary governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervention within a bloc is a Cold War question his sources never reach, so neutral.

corporate-influence.rationale: He was anti-capitalist and attacked the Republic's financial and political elites, which supports agreement that business sways government.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nationalists of his era feared depopulation and valued the family, so state incentives are a reasonable inference.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: His doctrine rests on authority, order and tradition, so a denial of any duty to obey law contradicts it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He grouped Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as the confederated states of 'anti-France' and linked the Dreyfus affair to Jewish influence.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage as a social institution is part of the family order he defended, so abolishing it contradicts his doctrine.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency law is not in his sources; neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: He favored hierarchical leagues and a disciplined movement, not trust-based informal groups, so a mild disagreement.

religious-nation.rationale: Maurras was agnostic and defined the nation historically, though Catholicism is a criterion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He was hostile to German hegemony and wanted France to be independent, so tributary deference contradicts his stance.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Communism's property distinction is not his concern; he opposed collective ownership of production, so neutral on this formula.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He was staunchly opposed to capitalism, and linked liberal modernity to decline, so he would not call it progressive.

cooperative-communities.rationale: His organic local order resembles self-governing communities, but he rejected collectivist cooperatives and utopianism, so a mild disagreement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Maurras is described as staunchly opposed to both capitalism and communism, favoring corporatism as a third course.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Maurras died in 1952 and the cited sources record no view of his on the Holocaust, so this is only a default disagreement.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He valued Catholicism as social order but was agnostic and not a theocrat, so it is a split matter.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He opposed colonial expansion but not specified.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He was no theocrat, and valued Catholicism only politically, so he would not remove rulers for lack of religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He rejected democracy and favored hierarchy, so direct participation in decisions contradicts his doctrine.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; his corporatist view was that trades give dignity, so he would not adopt it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Legitimacy rested on reason not divine right.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He valued the army and wanted France strong against Germany, so abolition is the opposite of his position.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He backed alliances such as the one against Germany, so a neutral stance goes against his diplomacy.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He denounced the republican press as venal, but his broader aim was not equal access, so neutral.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He wanted a strong state with order and authority, so abolition contradicts his doctrine.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His Catholic and subsidiarist social order leaves local and church bodies a role, so a mild lean toward agreement.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a democratic device he rejected.

proportional-representation.rationale: He rejected party-based parliaments in favour of a king and councils of corporate and local representatives.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Maurras endorsed violence, war and political killing in the national interest, so no absolute bar on killing.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Maurras grounded France in a continuous inherited tradition from the Capetian monarchy, set against the Revolution's break with it.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maurras's politics-first empiricism treats politics as a science of order and national interest, though he saw Catholicism as social order.

culture-before-state.rationale: Politics first (politique d'abord) means restoring the monarchic state before anything else, the opposite of culture first.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Maurras treated Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as anti-France and wanted them kept out of national life.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Action française was anti-socialist and rejected class struggle, so workers' own political power is not the test of a sound order.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Maurras wanted regional liberties granted and guarded by a hereditary monarch, not assemblies whose delegates only coordinate.

person-over-state.rationale: Maurras subordinated the individual to the nation, treating liberal individual rights as a source of decay.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as a social order and tradition, not as personal faith, so support is real but mild.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Maurras favoured regional liberties under the monarch, but the question about a national legislature's powers does not fit a monarchy without parliament.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Maurras rejected biological racism in favour of national and cultural exclusion, so organising by race is not his basis, though he named groups as 'anti-France'.

racial-pride.rationale: Maurras's pride was in the nation, its Catholic and Latin heritage, not in race as such.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Maurras treated foreigners and the 'four confederated states' as agents working against France, and was fixated on Germany weakening the country.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Integral nationalism treats the army and national defence as supreme goods, so refusing orders in inter-state war runs against it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement's corporatist and national-syndicalist leanings favoured organised trades and professional bodies settling conditions over liberal individual contracts.

sacred-nation.rationale: Maurras held the nation to be a hereditary patrimony of the dead and the living, a community greater than individuals.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Maurras was an agnostic who valued Catholicism as the historic French order, not as one expression of a universal truth; he ranked Catholic France above other creeds.

workers-own-party.rationale: It rejected parties, parliamentarism and class struggle, wanting workers organised in national corporations under the monarchy rather than in their own party.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Maurras valued Catholicism as the social order of France and wanted it privileged, while treating Protestants and Jews as 'anti-France', so equal legal standing is rejected.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Maurras attacked parliamentary democracy and held legitimacy comes from results and heredity, so he would deny that elections alone make a government legitimate; read as a definition, adherents might partly accept it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Maurras defended Catholicism as the guarantor of social order and the family, so blaming religion for women's oppression runs against his doctrine.

national-church-status.rationale: Action française held Catholicism should be the state religion with special legal status; the movement's position is documented.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Maurras's nationalisme intégral rooted the nation in la terre et les morts, the inherited soil and ancestors, which present generations must preserve.

self-ownership.rationale: Maurras held that the individual is a product of family, nation and tradition, and rejected the liberal individualism of the Revolution; self-ownership as an absolute right runs against this.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Enquête sur la monarchie argues for a hereditary king standing over parties, and Maurras attacked party politics and the republican regime as dividing the nation.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Maurras championed Catholicism as the social order of France, a Catholic politique even as an unbeliever, and Action française defended Catholic place in public life, though he opposed confessional parties.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Maurras's traditionalism sought order and tradition on modern France, accepting industrial modernity under a monarchy while restoring inherited institutions.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Action française pursued national-syndicalist appeals to workers, linking national loyalty to protecting their interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Maurras was an anti-communist who rejected party rule and Marxism in favour of monarchy.

missingStatements.text: The nation's enemies include groups within it, such as religious or ethnic minorities, who should be treated as foreign to the nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Maurras grouped Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as the 'four confederated states' of anti-France, and urged state action against them.

missingStatements.text: A country's real communities of family, locality and trade matter more than its formal political institutions.
missingStatements.rationale: The pays réel against the pays légal is a central Maurrassian distinction.

notes: Maurras was agnostic until near his death and valued Catholicism politically, which led the Vatican to condemn the movement in 1926-27 (lifted in 1939). Many answers on modern issues are inferred at low confidence.
